subject.title: fix(release): repair plugin prerelease contract gates

question: Should explicit Gateway session creation adopt the proposed fail-fast `UNAVAILABLE` behavior instead of waiting when a trusted initializer has already persisted an initializing target row?
rationale: This is a deliberate caller-visible availability and retry-contract change on a protected release PR; focused tests support the implementation, but maintainer acceptance and real lifecycle proof should confirm the intended operational behavior.

options.title: Accept with live lifecycle proof
options.body: Keep the fail-fast branch after a redacted terminal or runtime transcript shows prompt rejection during initialization and successful retry after initialization completes.

options.title: Keep waiting semantics
options.body: Reject the behavior change and retain the existing fence-wait contract if callers are expected to wait rather than handle a retryable unavailable error.

recommendation.title: Accept with live lifecycle proof
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-fast branch after a redacted terminal or runtime transcript shows prompt rejection during initialization and successful retry after initialization completes.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence ties steipete to this release-validation repair and its intended session-create contract.
